about.title: About CORE
about.intro: We believe in setting a great example for others.
about.detail: CORE describes its team as people from different places and backgrounds working toward the same aim: a community that supports Scholars and families with equity, accountability, partnership, and kindness.

sections.heading: Work with purpose
body: CORE says every young person deserves the opportunity, support, and experiences needed to build a successful future. Staff work alongside Scholars, families, schools, and community partners across academic support, character development, career exploration, and financial literacy.

sections.heading: Careers at CORE
body: The current site invites applicants who value collaboration and community and who believe in the potential of every Scholar. CORE states that it is an equal opportunity employer.

sections.heading: Alumni voice
body: “CORE gave me the courage and skills to set higher expectations for myself. I wouldn’t be where I am today if it wasn’t for the program and the people.”

sections.heading: Financial transparency
body: The current site links financial documents for 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2024, and 2025 and states that CORE is a tax-exempt public charity in good standing under Section 501(c)(3).

contact.title: Contact CORE
contact.intro: Have a question about programs, participation, partnerships, volunteering, or support?
contact.detail: The public source site lists CORE at 701 S. 9th Street, Las Vegas, NV 89101, (702) 657-3264, and info@corewecan.org.

sections.heading: General contact
body: Email info@corewecan.org or call (702) 657-3264. Families asking about joining are directed by the current FAQ to family@corewecan.org.

sections.heading: Areas of interest
body: The existing involvement form asks whether someone is interested in mentoring, donating, volunteering, fundraising, or taking a tour. The rebuilt site will connect these actions to GHL forms after the final CRM destinations are approved.

character-development.title: Character Development
character-development.intro: We help Scholars build the character, confidence, and life skills they need to thrive in school, their communities, and future careers.
character-development.detail: CORE combines character curriculum, service learning, collaborative activities, and real-world experiences so Scholars can practice the skills behind strong decisions, relationships, resilience, and citizenship.

sections.heading: Community Service & Service Learning
body: Giving back is one of the ways CORE helps young people discover their potential. Scholars partner with local nonprofits and community organizations to identify needs, plan service projects, and make a meaningful difference throughout Southern Nevada.
The current source page states that each Scholar completes 50 hours of community service annually.

sections.heading: Character Development curriculum
body: CORE’s after-school curriculum uses interactive lessons, discussions, collaborative activities, and real-world experiences.

sections.heading: Practice, not just theory
body: CORE describes character as something students build through repeated opportunities to practice communication, problem-solving, collaboration, emotional regulation, and ethical decision-making.

career-awareness.title: Career Awareness & Exploration
career-awareness.detail: CORE helps Scholars discover careers that match their interests, strengths, and goals through hands-on experiences, workplace learning, and meaningful connections with professionals.

sections.heading: Career We Can
body: Career We Can is CORE’s career awareness and exploration program. Since launching in 2018, the source site says it has connected students with professionals, workplace experiences, internships, and hands-on learning opportunities.

sections.heading: Make possibilities visible
body: Career exploration is framed as discovery rather than forcing students to choose a job today.
sections.quote: Students can't aspire to careers they've never seen. Career We Can helps make those possibilities visible.

financial-literacy.title: Financial Literacy
financial-literacy.intro: Build the knowledge and confidence to make smart financial decisions—for today and tomorrow.
financial-literacy.detail: CORE presents financial literacy as lifelong habits for making informed decisions, setting goals, and building brighter futures.

sections.heading: Financial literacy for Scholars
body: Learning good financial habits starts early. CORE’s current page highlights practical topics that prepare Scholars for high school, college, careers, and adulthood.

sections.heading: Supporting the whole family
body: CORE connects families with community organizations, educational institutions, and workforce development agencies that can strengthen financial stability, education, and career advancement. The source page mentions workforce training, GED pathways, higher education, and community resources.

sections.heading: Two-generation approach
body: CORE links student success and family success, treating education, career progress, and financial confidence as connected across generations.
